parts.text: In this experiment, you will determine the mass of a metre rule using two methods. Method 1. Carry out the following instructions, referring to Fig. 1.1. Fig. 1.1 You are provided with a 100 g mass, labelled X .

parts.label: i
parts.text: (a) (i) Place the mass X on the rule so that its centre is at a distance d = 5.0 cm from the zero end of the rule, as shown in Fig. 1.1. Record the value of d in Table 1.1.

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Adjust the position of the rule so that it is as near as possible to being balanced, with the 50.0 cm mark to the right of the pivot.

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Measure, and record in the table, the distance x from the centre of the mass X to the pivot.

parts.label: iv
parts.text: (iv) Measure, and record in the table, the distance y from the pivot to the 50.0 cm mark on the rule.

parts.label: v
parts.text: (v) Repeat the steps (i) – (iv) using d = 10.0 cm. Table 1.1 d /cm x /cm y /cm [3]

parts.label: i
parts.text: (b) (i) Using the values of x and y in the first row of the table, calculate the mass M of the rule using the equation M = 100 x y . M = ........................................[1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Repeat step (b)(i) using the values of x and y in the second row of the table. M = ........................................[1]

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Calculate the average value of M. average value of M = ........................................[1] Method 2.

ms.label: 1(b)(iii)
ms.text: (ignore sig. figs., but rounding must be correct)

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Measure the mass M of the rule using the balance provided. M = ........................................[1]
